problems.problem:
Consider a population with equal numbers of men and women, in which $5\%$ of the men and $0.25\%$ of the women are colour-blind. Give the probability that a colour-blind person selected at random from this population is a woman.

(A) $\dfrac{1}{21}$
(B) $\dfrac{1}{8}$
(C) $\dfrac{3}{21}$
(D) $\dfrac{5}{21}$
(E) $\dfrac{1}{4}$

Let $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{C}$ be such that $|\alpha| = |\beta| = 1$ and $|\alpha - \beta| = \sqrt{2}$. Then $\alpha^2 + \beta^2$ equals

(A) $-2$
(B) $0$
(C) $1$
(D) $2$
(E) $2i$

Consider the system $Ax = b$, where
$$A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 2 & k & 6 \\ -1 & 3 & k-3 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad b = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 6 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} \qquad \text{and} \qquad k \in \mathbb{R}.$$
Let $T$ be the sum of all values of $k$ that make the system inconsistent and let $S$ be the sum of all values of $k$ that make the system consistent with infinitely many solutions. Then the value of $T - S$ is

(A) $-4$
(B) $-3$
(C) $0$
(D) $1$
(E) $4$

Let $A$ and $C$ be invertible $n \times n$ matrices such that $\det(I + C^{-1}A) = 1/3$ and $\det A = 5$. Given that $B = 3\left(A^{-1} + C^{-1}\right)^t$, the determinant of $B$ equals

(A) $3^n$
(B) $2 \cdot \dfrac{3^n}{5^2}$
(C) $\dfrac{1}{5}$
(D) $\dfrac{3^{n-1}}{5}$
(E) $5 \cdot 3^{n-1}$

A polynomial $P$ is the product of $5$ polynomials whose degrees form a geometric progression. If the polynomial of least degree has degree $2$ and the degree of $P$ is $62$, then the one of greatest degree has degree

(A) $30$
(B) $32$
(C) $34$
(D) $36$
(E) $38$

A dihedral angle measures $120^\circ$. The distance from the edge of the dihedral angle to the centre of a sphere of volume $4\sqrt{3}\,\pi\ \text{cm}^3$ that is tangent to the faces of the dihedral angle is, in cm, equal to

(A) $3\sqrt{3}$
(B) $3\sqrt{2}$
(C) $2\sqrt{3}$
(D) $2\sqrt{2}$
(E) $2$

Consider the square $ABCD$ with sides of length $10\ \text{m}$. Let $M$ be a point on the side $\overline{AB}$ and $N$ a point on the side $\overline{AD}$, equidistant from $A$. Through $M$ draw a line $r$ parallel to the side $\overline{AD}$ and through $N$ a line $s$ parallel to the side $\overline{AB}$; they meet at the point $O$. Consider the squares $AMON$ and $OPCQ$, where $P$ is the intersection of $s$ with the side $\overline{BC}$ and $Q$ is the intersection of $r$ with the side $\overline{DC}$. Given that the areas of the squares $AMON$, $OPCQ$ and $ABCD$ form, in this order, a geometric progression, the distance between the points $A$ and $M$ is, in metres,

(A) $15 + 5\sqrt{5}$
(B) $10 + 5\sqrt{5}$
(C) $10 - \sqrt{5}$
(D) $15 - 5\sqrt{5}$
(E) $10 - 3\sqrt{5}$

Consider the polynomial $p(x) = a_5x^5 + a_4x^4 + a_3x^3 + a_2x^2 - a_1$, one of whose roots is $x = -1$. Given that $a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4$ and $a_5$ are real and form, in this order, an arithmetic progression with $a_4 = 1/2$, then $p(-2)$ equals

(A) $-25$
(B) $-27$
(C) $-36$
(D) $-39$
(E) $-40$

About the polynomial equation $2x^4 + ax^3 + bx^2 + cx - 1 = 0$ we know that the coefficients $a, b, c$ are real, two of its roots are distinct integers, and $1/2 - i/2$ is also a root. Then the maximum of $a, b, c$ equals

(A) $-1$
(B) $1$
(C) $2$
(D) $3$
(E) $4$

The polynomial equation
$$(a + c + 2)\,x^3 + (b + 3c + 1)\,x^2 + (c - a)\,x + (a + b + 4) = 0$$
is given, with $a, b, c$ real. Given that this equation is reciprocal of the first kind and that $1$ is a root, the product $abc$ equals

(A) $-2$
(B) $4$
(C) $6$
(D) $9$
(E) $12$

Taking $[-\pi/2, \pi/2]$ as the range of the arcsine function and $[0, \pi]$ as the range of the arccosine function, find the value of
$$\cos\left(\arcsin\frac{3}{5} + \arccos\frac{4}{5}\right).$$

(A) $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{12}}$
(B) $\dfrac{7}{25}$
(C) $\dfrac{4}{15}$
(D) $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{15}}$
(E) $\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}$

Given the conic $\lambda : x^2 - y^2 = 1$, which of the lines below is perpendicular to $\lambda$ at the point $P = \left(2, \sqrt{3}\right)$?

(A) $y = \sqrt{3}(x - 1)$
(B) $y = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}x$
(C) $y = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}(x + 1)$
(D) $y = \dfrac{-\sqrt{3}}{5}(x - 7)$
(E) $y = \dfrac{-\sqrt{3}}{2}(x - 4)$

The range and the period of $f(x) = 2\sin^2(3x) + \sin(6x) - 1$ are, respectively,

(A) $[-3, 3]$ and $2\pi$
(B) $[-2, 2]$ and $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$
(C) $\left[-\sqrt{2}, \sqrt{2}\right]$ and $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$
(D) $[-1, 3]$ and $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$
(E) $[-1, 3]$ and $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

For $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the solution set of $\left|5^{3x} - 5^{2x+1} + 4 \cdot 5^x\right| = |5^x - 1|$ is

(A) $\left\{0,\ 2 \pm \sqrt{5},\ 2 \pm \sqrt{3}\right\}$
(B) $\left\{0,\ 1,\ \log_5\left(2 + \sqrt{5}\right)\right\}$
(C) $\left\{0,\ \frac{1}{2}\log_5 2,\ \frac{1}{2}\log_5 3,\ \log_5\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\right\}$
(D) $\left\{0,\ \log_5\left(2 + \sqrt{5}\right),\ \log_5\left(2 + \sqrt{3}\right),\ \log_5\left(2 - \sqrt{3}\right)\right\}$
(E) The only solution is $x = 0$

A subset $D$ of $\mathbb{R}$ such that the function $f : D \to \mathbb{R}$ defined by $f(x) = \left|\ln\left(x^2 - x + 1\right)\right|$ is injective is

(A) $\mathbb{R}$
(B) $(-\infty, 1]$
(C) $[0, 1/2]$
(D) $(0, 1)$
(E) $[1/2, \infty)$

The sum of all the distinct solutions of the equation
$$\cos 3x + 2\cos 6x + \cos 9x = 0$$
that lie in the interval $0 \le x \le \pi/2$ equals

(A) $2\pi$
(B) $\dfrac{23}{12}\pi$
(C) $\dfrac{9}{6}\pi$
(D) $\dfrac{7}{6}\pi$
(E) $\dfrac{13}{12}\pi$

Consider the set $D = \{n \in \mathbb{N};\ 1 \le n \le 365\}$ and let $H \subset \mathcal{P}(D)$ consist of all the subsets of $D$ with $2$ elements. Choosing an element $B \in H$ at random, the probability that the sum of its elements is $183$ equals

(A) $\dfrac{1}{730}$
(B) $\dfrac{46}{33\,215}$
(C) $\dfrac{1}{365}$
(D) $\dfrac{92}{33\,215}$
(E) $\dfrac{91}{730}$

Consider the isosceles triangle $ABC$ in which the angle different from the others, $B\hat{A}C$, measures $40^\circ$. On the side $\overline{AB}$ take the point $E$ such that $A\hat{C}E = 15^\circ$. On the side $\overline{AC}$ take the point $D$ such that $D\hat{B}C = 35^\circ$. Then the angle $E\hat{D}B$ measures

(A) $35^\circ$
(B) $45^\circ$
(C) $55^\circ$
(D) $75^\circ$
(E) $85^\circ$

Let $X, Y, Z, W$ be subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ such that $(X - Y) \cap Z = \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$, $Y = \{5, 6\}$, $Z \cap Y = \emptyset$, $W \cap (X - Z) = \{7, 8\}$, $X \cap W \cap Z = \{2, 4\}$. Then the set $[X \cap (Z \cup W)] - [W \cap (Y \cup Z)]$ equals

(A) $\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$
(B) $\{1, 2, 3, 4, 7\}$
(C) $\{1, 3, 7, 8\}$
(D) $\{1, 3\}$
(E) $\{7, 8\}$

Let $r$ and $s$ be two parallel lines at distance $10\ \text{cm}$ from each other. Let $P$ be a point in the plane defined by $r$ and $s$, outside the region bounded by these lines, at distance $5\ \text{cm}$ from $r$. The area and the perimeter, in $\text{cm}^2$ and cm respectively, of the equilateral triangle $PQR$ whose vertices $Q$ and $R$ lie on the lines $r$ and $s$, respectively, are

(A) $175\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$ and $5\sqrt{21}$
(B) $175\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$ and $10\sqrt{21}$
(C) $175\sqrt{3}$ and $10\sqrt{21}$
(D) $175\sqrt{3}$ and $5\sqrt{21}$
(E) $700$ and $10\sqrt{21}$
Given the set $A = \left\{x \in \mathbb{R};\ \sqrt{3x^2 + 2x} < x^2\right\}$, express it as a union of intervals of the real line.

Determine the roots in $\mathbb{C}$ of $4z^6 + 256 = 0$, in the form $a + bi$ with $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$, that belong to
$$S = \{z \in \mathbb{C};\ 1 < |z + 2| < 3\}.$$

Let $f(x) = \ln\left(x^2 + x + 1\right)$, $x \in \mathbb{R}$. Determine the functions $h, g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $f(x) = g(x) + h(x)$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$, where $h$ is an even function and $g$ is an odd function.

Let $\alpha, \beta, \gamma \in \mathbb{R}$. Consider the polynomial $p(x)$ given by
$$x^5 - 9x^4 + (\alpha - \beta - 2\gamma)\,x^3 + (\alpha + 2\beta + 2\gamma - 2)\,x^2 + (\alpha - \beta - \gamma + 1)\,x + (2\alpha + \beta + \gamma - 1).$$
Find all values of $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ such that $x = 0$ is a root of multiplicity $3$ of $p(x)$.

A real square matrix $A$ is orthogonal if $A$ is invertible and $A^{-1} = A^t$. Determine all $2 \times 2$ matrices that are symmetric and orthogonal, expressing them, where appropriate, in terms of their entries off the main diagonal.

Determine all values $\alpha \in \left]\dfrac{-\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right[$ such that the equation (in $x$)
$$x^4 - 2\sqrt[4]{3}\,x^2 + \tan\alpha = 0$$
has only simple real roots.

In a sample space with a probability $P$, events $A$, $B$ and $C$ are given such that $P(A) = P(B) = 1/2$, with $A$ and $B$ independent, $P(A \cap B \cap C) = 1/16$, and it is known that $P((A \cap B) \cup (A \cap C)) = 3/10$. Compute the conditional probabilities $P(C \mid A \cap B)$ and $P\left(C \mid A \cap B^C\right)$.

An acute triangle with vertices $A$, $B$ and $C$ is inscribed in a circle of radius $\dfrac{5\sqrt{2}}{3}$. It is known that $\overline{AB}$ measures $2\sqrt{5}$ and $\overline{BC}$ measures $2\sqrt{2}$. Determine the area of the triangle $ABC$.

Let $C$ be a circle of radius $r$ and centre $O$, and let $\overline{AB}$ be a diameter of $C$. Consider the equilateral triangle $BDE$ inscribed in $C$. The line $s$ through the points $O$ and $E$ is drawn until it meets, at $F$, the line $t$ tangent to the circle $C$ at the point $A$. Determine the volume of the solid of revolution generated by rotating the region bounded by the arc $\overset{\frown}{AE}$ and the segments $\overline{AF}$ and $\overline{EF}$ about the diameter $\overline{AB}$.

Consider the parabola with equation $y = ax^2 + bx + c$ that passes through the points $(2, 5)$, $(-1, 2)$ and is such that $a, b, c$ form, in this order, an arithmetic progression. Determine the distance from the vertex of the parabola to the line tangent to the parabola at the point $(2, 5)$.

Let $A$ and $B$ be subsets of the universal set $U = \{a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h\}$. Given that $(B^C \cup A)^C = \{f, g, h\}$, $B^C \cap A = \{a, b\}$ and $A^C \setminus B = \{d, e\}$, then $n(P(A \cap B))$ equals

(A) $0$.
(B) $1$.
(C) $2$.
(D) $4$.
(E) $8$.

A company owns $1000$ cars, some with petrol engines and the rest with "flex" engines (which run on both ethanol and petrol). At a certain time, among these $1000$ cars, $36\%$ of the petrol-engine cars and $36\%$ of the flex-engine cars are converted so that they also run on natural gas (CNG). Given that, after this conversion, $556$ of the company's $1000$ cars are bi-fuel, one can state that the number of tri-fuel cars is

(A) $246$.
(B) $252$.
(C) $260$.
(D) $268$.
(E) $284$.

Let $f : \mathbb{R} \longrightarrow \mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$ be a function satisfying the conditions:
$$f(x + y) = f(x)\,f(y) \ \text{ for all } x, y \in \mathbb{R} \qquad \text{and} \qquad f(x) \ne 1 \ \text{ for all } x \in \mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}.$$
Of the statements:
I. $f$ can be odd.
II. $f(0) = 1$.
III. $f$ is injective.
IV. $f$ is not surjective, since $f(x) > 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$.
the false one(s) is (are) only

(A) I and III.
(B) II and III.
(C) I and IV.
(D) IV.
(E) I.

If $a = \cos\dfrac{\pi}{5}$ and $b = \sin\dfrac{\pi}{5}$, then the complex number $\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{5} + i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{5}\right)^{54}$ equals

(A) $a + bi$.
(B) $-a + bi$.
(C) $(1 - 2a^2b^2) + ab(1 + b^2)i$.
(D) $a - bi$.
(E) $1 - 4a^2b^2 + 2ab(1 - b^2)i$.

The polynomial of degree $4$
$$(a + 2b + c)x^4 + (a + b + c)x^3 - (a - b)x^2 + (2a - b + c)x + 2(a + c),$$
with $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$, is an even function. Then the sum of the moduli of its roots equals

(A) $3 + \sqrt{3}$.
(B) $2 + 3\sqrt{3}$.
(C) $2 + \sqrt{2}$.
(D) $1 + 2\sqrt{2}$.
(E) $2 + 2\sqrt{2}$.

Consider the functions $f(x) = x^4 + 2x^3 - 2x - 1$ and $g(x) = x^2 - 2x + 1$. The multiplicity of the non-real roots of the composite function $f \circ g$ equals

(A) $1$.
(B) $2$.
(C) $3$.
(D) $4$.
(E) $5$.

Suppose that the real coefficients $a$ and $b$ of the equation $x^4 + ax^3 + bx^2 + ax + 1 = 0$ are such that the equation has a non-real solution $r$ with $|r| \ne 1$. Of the following statements:
I. The equation has four distinct roots, all of them non-real.
II. The roots can be double.
III. Of the four roots, two can be real.
the true one(s) is (are)

(A) only I.
(B) only II.
(C) only III.
(D) only II and III.
(E) none.

If the solutions of the algebraic equation $2x^3 - ax^2 + bx + 54 = 0$, with coefficients $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$, $b \ne 0$, form, in some order, a geometric progression, then $\dfrac{a}{b}$ equals

(A) $-3$.
(B) $-\dfrac{1}{3}$.
(C) $\dfrac{1}{3}$.
(D) $1$.
(E) $3$.

Given $A \in M_{3\times 2}(\mathbb{R})$ and $b \in M_{3\times 1}(\mathbb{R})$, we say that $X_0 \in M_{2\times 1}(\mathbb{R})$ is the best quadratic approximation of the system $AX = b$ when $\sqrt{(AX_0 - b)^t(AX_0 - b)}$ takes the least possible value. Then, given the system
$$\begin{bmatrix} -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix},$$
its best quadratic approximation is

(A) $\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}$.
(B) $\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$.
(C) $\begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$.
(D) $\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$.
(E) $\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$.

The system
$$\begin{cases} a_1x + b_1y = c_1 \\ a_2x + b_2y = c_2 \end{cases}, \qquad a_1, a_2, b_1, b_2, c_1, c_2 \in \mathbb{R},$$
with $(c_1, c_2) \ne (0, 0)$ and $a_1c_1 + a_2c_2 = b_1c_1 + b_2c_2 = 0$, is

(A) consistent with a unique solution.
(B) consistent with a unique solution only when $c_1 \ne 0$ and $c_2 \ne 0$.
(C) consistent with a unique solution only when $c_1 \ne 0$ and $c_2 = 0$, or $c_1 = 0$ and $c_2 \ne 0$.
(D) inconsistent.
(E) consistent with infinitely many solutions.

Let $A \in M_{2\times 2}(\mathbb{R})$ be a nonzero symmetric matrix whose entries are such that $a_{11}$, $a_{12}$ and $a_{22}$ form, in this order, a geometric progression with ratio $q \ne 1$, and $\operatorname{tr} A = 5a_{11}$. Given that the system $AX = X$ has a nonzero solution $X \in M_{2\times 1}(\mathbb{R})$, one can state that $a_{11}^2 + q^2$ equals

(A) $\dfrac{101}{25}$.
(B) $\dfrac{121}{25}$.
(C) $5$.
(D) $\dfrac{49}{9}$.
(E) $\dfrac{25}{4}$.

A certain English exam is used to classify the proficiency of foreigners in this language. Of the foreigners who are proficient in English, $75\%$ are rated well in this exam. Among those not proficient in English, $7\%$ are nevertheless rated well. Consider a sample of foreigners in which $18\%$ are proficient in English. A foreigner chosen at random from this sample took the exam and was classified as proficient in English. The probability that this foreigner is actually proficient in the language is approximately

(A) $73\%$.
(B) $70\%$.
(C) $68\%$.
(D) $65\%$.
(E) $64\%$.

Consider the triangle $ABC$ with sides $a = \overline{BC}$, $b = \overline{AC}$ and $c = \overline{AB}$ and interior angles $\alpha = C\widehat{A}B$, $\beta = A\widehat{B}C$ and $\gamma = B\widehat{C}A$. Given that the equation $x^2 - 2bx\cos\alpha + b^2 - a^2 = 0$ has $c$ as a double root, one can state that

(A) $\alpha = 90^\circ$.
(B) $\beta = 60^\circ$.
(C) $\gamma = 90^\circ$.
(D) The triangle is right-angled only if $\alpha = 45^\circ$.
(E) The triangle is right-angled and $b$ is the hypotenuse.

In the plane, let $S$ be the locus of the points for which the sum of the squares of their distances to the line $t : x = 1$ and to the point $A = (3, 2)$ equals $4$. Then $S$ is

(A) a circle of radius $\sqrt{2}$ and centre $(2, 1)$.
(B) a circle of radius $1$ and centre $(1, 2)$.
(C) a hyperbola.
(D) an ellipse with axes of lengths $2\sqrt{2}$ and $2$.
(E) an ellipse with axes of lengths $2$ and $1$.

Of the triangle with vertices $A$, $B$ and $C$, inscribed in a circle of radius $R = 2\ \text{cm}$, it is known that the side $\overline{BC}$ measures $2\ \text{cm}$ and the interior angle $A\widehat{B}C$ measures $30^\circ$. Then the radius of the circle inscribed in this triangle has length, in cm, equal to

(A) $2 - \sqrt{3}$.
(B) $\dfrac{1}{3}$.
(C) $\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{4}$.
(D) $2\sqrt{3} - 3$.
(E) $\dfrac{1}{2}$.

The distance between the vertex and the focus of the parabola with equation $2x^2 - 4x - 4y + 3 = 0$ equals

(A) $2$.
(B) $\dfrac{3}{2}$.
(C) $1$.
(D) $\dfrac{3}{4}$.
(E) $\dfrac{1}{2}$.

The expression
$$\frac{2\left[\sin\left(x + \frac{11}{2}\pi\right) + \cot^2 x\right]\tan\frac{x}{2}}{1 + \tan^2\frac{x}{2}}$$
is equivalent to

(A) $\left[\cos x - \sin^2 x\right]\cot x$.
(B) $\left[\sin x + \cos x\right]\tan x$.
(C) $\left[\cos^2 x - \sin x\right]\cot^2 x$.
(D) $\left[1 - \cot^2 x\right]\sin x$.
(E) $\left[1 + \cot^2 x\right]\left[\sin x + \cos x\right]$.

Let $C$ be a circle of radius $R > 4$ and centre $(0, 0)$, and let $\overline{AB}$ be a chord of $C$. Given that $(1, 3)$ is the midpoint of $\overline{AB}$, an equation of the line containing $\overline{AB}$ is

(A) $y + 3x - 6 = 0$.
(B) $3y + x - 10 = 0$.
(C) $2y + x - 7 = 0$.
(D) $y + x - 4 = 0$.
(E) $2y + 3x - 9 = 0$.

A sphere is placed inside a right circular cone of height $8\ \text{cm}$ and vertex angle $60^\circ$. The points of contact of the sphere with the lateral surface of the cone form a circle and are at distance $2\sqrt{3}\ \text{cm}$ from the vertex of the cone. The volume of the cone not occupied by the sphere, in $\text{cm}^3$, equals

(A) $\dfrac{416}{9}\pi$.
(B) $\dfrac{480}{9}\pi$.
(C) $\dfrac{500}{9}\pi$.
(D) $\dfrac{512}{9}\pi$.
(E) $\dfrac{542}{9}\pi$.

The points $A = (3, 4)$ and $B = (4, 3)$ are vertices of a cube, of which $\overline{AB}$ is one of the edges. The lateral area of the octahedron whose vertices are the midpoints of the faces of the cube equals

(A) $\sqrt{8}$.
(B) $3$.
(C) $\sqrt{12}$.
(D) $4$.
(E) $\sqrt{18}$.

Let $S$ be the solution set of the inequality
$$(x - 9)\left|\log_{x+4}\left(x^3 - 26x\right)\right| \le 0.$$
Determine the set $S^C$.

Let $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$ and $w = x^2(1 + 3i) + y^2(4 - i) - x(2 + 6i) + y(-16 + 4i) \in \mathbb{C}$. Identify and sketch the set
$$\Omega = \{(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2;\ \operatorname{Re} w \le -13 \ \text{and}\ \operatorname{Im} w \le 4\}.$$

Let $f : \mathbb{R}\setminus\{-1\} \to \mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x) = \dfrac{2x + 3}{x + 1}$.
a) Show that $f$ is injective.
b) Determine $D = \{f(x);\ x \in \mathbb{R}\setminus\{-1\}\}$ and $f^{-1} : D \to \mathbb{R}\setminus\{-1\}$.

Suppose that the algebraic equation
$$x^{11} + \sum_{n=1}^{10} a_nx^n + a_0 = 0$$
has real coefficients $a_0, a_1, \ldots, a_{10}$ such that its eleven roots are all simple and of the form $\beta + i\gamma_n$, where $\beta, \gamma_n \in \mathbb{R}$ and the $\gamma_n$, $n = 1, 2, \ldots, 11$, form an arithmetic progression with real common difference $\gamma \ne 0$. Consider the three statements below and answer whether each of them is, respectively, true or false, justifying your answer:
I. If $\beta = 0$, then $a_0 = 0$.
II. If $a_{10} = 0$, then $\beta = 0$.
III. If $\beta = 0$, then $a_1 = 0$.

A certain competitive examination is held in two stages. Over recent years, $20\%$ of the candidates have obtained, in the first stage, a mark greater than or equal to the minimum mark needed to take part in the second stage. If we take $6$ candidates from among the many registered, what is the probability that at least $4$ of them obtain a mark allowing them to take part in the second stage?

Let $A, B \in M_{3\times 3}(\mathbb{R})$. Prove the properties below:
a) If $AX$ is the zero column matrix for every $X \in M_{3\times 1}(\mathbb{R})$, then $A$ is the zero matrix.
b) If $A$ and $B$ are nonzero and such that $AB$ is the zero matrix, then $\det A = \det B = 0$.
Given that $\tan^2\left(x + \dfrac{1}{6}\pi\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$ for some $x \in \left[0, \dfrac{1}{2}\pi\right]$, determine $\sin x$.

Given the circle $C : (x - 3)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 20$ and the line $r : 3x - y + 5 = 0$, consider the line $t$ that is tangent to $C$, makes an angle of $45^\circ$ with $r$, and whose distance to the origin is $\dfrac{3\sqrt{5}}{5}$. Determine an equation of the line $t$.

Consider the $n$ lines
$$r_i : y = m_ix + 10, \quad i = 1, 2, \ldots, n; \quad n \ge 5,$$
where the coefficients $m_i$, in increasing order of $i$, form an arithmetic progression with common difference $q > 0$. If $m_1 = 0$ and the line $r_5$ is tangent to the circle with equation $x^2 + y^2 = 25$, determine the value of $q$.
The ratio between the lateral area and the area of the octagonal base of a regular pyramid equals $\sqrt{5}$. Express the volume of this pyramid in terms of the length $a$ of the apothem of the base.

Consider the statements below about arbitrary sets $A$, $B$ and $C$:
I. The negation of $x \in A \cap B$ is: $x \notin A$ or $x \notin B$.
II. $A \cap (B \cup C) = (A \cap B) \cup (A \cap C)$.

Consider sets $A, B \subset \mathbb{R}$ and $C \subset (A \cup B)$. If $A \cup B$, $A \cap C$ and $B \cap C$ are the domains of the real functions defined by $\ln\left(x - \sqrt{\pi}\right)$, $\sqrt{-x^2 + 6x - 8}$ and $\sqrt{\dfrac{x - \pi}{5 - x}}$, respectively, one can state that

The principal arguments of the solutions of the equation in $z$

belong to

Consider the arithmetic progression $(a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{50})$ with common difference $d$. If $\sum_{n=1}^{10} a_n = 10 + 25d$ and $\sum_{n=1}^{50} a_n = 4550$, then $d - a_1$ equals

An equilateral triangle has its vertices at the points $A$, $B$ and $C$ of the $xOy$ plane, where $B = (2, 1)$ and $C = (5, 5)$. Of the following statements:

Let $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ be the vertices of a regular tetrahedron whose edges measure $1\ \text{cm}$. If $M$ is the midpoint of the segment $\overline{AB}$ and $N$ is the midpoint of the segment $\overline{CD}$, then the area of the triangle $MND$, in $\text{cm}^2$, equals

III. $a_0 < 0$.

A lottery urn contains $90$ balls numbered from $1$ to $90$, each ball being equally likely to be drawn.

Consider the matrices $A \in M_{4\times 4}(\mathbb{R})$ and $X, B \in M_{4\times 1}(\mathbb{R})$:
$$A = \begin{bmatrix} a & 1 & b & 1 \\ b & 1 & a & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ -a & 2 & b & 1 \end{bmatrix}; \quad X = \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \\ w \end{bmatrix} \quad \text{and} \quad B = \begin{bmatrix} b_1 \\ b_2 \\ b_3 \\ b_4 \end{bmatrix}.$$

Let $z = n^2(\cos 45^\circ + i\sin 45^\circ)$ and $w = n(\cos 15^\circ + i\sin 15^\circ)$, where $n$ is the least positive integer such that $(1 + i)^n$ is real. Then $\dfrac{z}{w}$ equals

If $\arg z = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, then a value of $\arg(-2iz)$ is

Let $r_1$, $r_2$ and $r_3$ be real numbers such that $r_1 - r_2$ and $r_1 + r_2 + r_3$ are rational. Of the statements:

The roots $x_1$, $x_2$ and $x_3$ of the polynomial $p(x) = 16 + ax - (4 + \sqrt{2})x^2 + x^3$ are related by the equations:

It is known that $(x + 2y,\ 3x - 5y,\ 8x - 2y,\ 11x - 7y + 2z)$ is an arithmetic progression whose last term equals $-127$. Then the product $xyz$ equals

Consider a polynomial $p(x)$ of degree $5$ with real coefficients. It is known that $-2i$ and $i - \sqrt{3}$ are two of its roots. It is also known that dividing $p(x)$ by the polynomial $q(x) = x - 5$ gives remainder zero and that $p(1) = 20(5 + 2\sqrt{3})$. Then $p(-1)$ equals

A triangle $ABC$ has sides of lengths $a = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\ \text{cm}$, $b = 1\ \text{cm}$ and $c = \dfrac{1}{2}\ \text{cm}$. Then the radius of the circle, in cm, equals

(D) $\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.

Let $A = (0, 0)$, $B = (0, 6)$ and $C = (4, 3)$ be the vertices of a triangle. The distance from the centroid of this triangle to the vertex $A$, in units of length, equals

(A) $\dfrac{5}{3}$.
(B) $\dfrac{\sqrt{97}}{3}$.
(C) $\dfrac{\sqrt{109}}{3}$.
(D) $\dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{3}$.

The area of the quadrilateral determined by the coordinate axes and the lines $r : x - 3y + 3 = 0$ and $s : 3x + y - 21 = 0$, in units of area, equals

(A) $\dfrac{19}{2}$.
(B) $10$.
(C) $\dfrac{25}{2}$.

(E) $\dfrac{29}{2}$.

Given the points $A = (0, 0)$, $B = (2, 0)$ and $C = (1, 1)$, the locus of the points at distance $d = 2$ from the internal bisector, through $A$, of the triangle $ABC$ is a pair of lines given by

(A) $r_{1,2} : \sqrt{2}\,y - x \pm 2\sqrt{4 + \sqrt{2}} = 0$.

Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ be subsets of a universal set $U$. Of the statements:

the one(s) that is (are) always true is (are) only

Let $A$ and $B$ be two disjoint sets, both finite and non-empty, such that $n(P(A) \cup P(B)) + 1 = n(P(A \cup B))$. Then the difference $n(A) - n(B)$ can take

(A) a single value.
(B) only two distinct values.

(D) only four distinct values.

Consider a fixed positive real number $a \ne 1$ and the equation in $x$
$$a^{2x} + 2\beta a^x - \beta = 0, \quad \beta \in \mathbb{R}.$$
Of the statements:

Let $S = \left\{x \in \mathbb{R} \;\middle|\; \arcsin\left(\dfrac{e^{-x} - e^x}{2}\right) + \arccos\left(\dfrac{e^x - e^{-x}}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right\}$. Then

(B) $S = \{0\}$.

(D) $S = \mathbb{R}^+$.
(E) $S = \mathbb{R}$.

Let $x \in [0, 2\pi]$ be such that $\sin(x)\cos(x) = \dfrac{2}{5}$. Then the product and the sum of all possible values of $\tan(x)$ are, respectively,

(A) $1$ and $0$.
(B) $1$ and $\dfrac{5}{2}$.
(C) $-1$ and $0$.
(D) $1$ and $5$.
(E) $-1$ and $-\dfrac{5}{2}$.

The sum $\sum_{k=0}^{n}\cos(\alpha + k\pi)$, for every $\alpha \in [0, 2\pi]$, equals

(A) $-\cos(\alpha)$ when $n$ is even.
(B) $-\sin(\alpha)$ when $n$ is odd.
(C) $\cos(\alpha)$ when $n$ is odd.
(D) $\sin(\alpha)$ when $n$ is even.
(E) zero when $n$ is odd.

A right circular cone of height $1\ \text{cm}$ and slant height $\dfrac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}\ \text{cm}$ is cut by a plane parallel to its base, which determines a new cone. For this new cone to have the same volume as a cube of edge $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{243}\right)^{1/3}\ \text{cm}$, the distance from the plane to the base of the original cone must be, in cm,

(A) $\dfrac{1}{4}$.
(B) $\dfrac{1}{3}$.
(C) $\dfrac{1}{2}$.
(D) $\dfrac{2}{3}$.
(E) $\dfrac{3}{4}$.

The lateral surface of a right circular cone is a circular sector of $120^\circ$ with area $3\pi\ \text{cm}^2$. The total surface area and the volume of this cone measure, in $\text{cm}^2$ and $\text{cm}^3$ respectively,

(A) $4\pi$ and $\dfrac{2\pi\sqrt{2}}{3}$.
(B) $4\pi$ and $\dfrac{\pi\sqrt{2}}{3}$.
(C) $4\pi$ and $\pi\sqrt{2}$.
(D) $3\pi$ and $\dfrac{2\pi\sqrt{2}}{3}$.
(E) $\pi$ and $2\pi\sqrt{2}$.
Ten cards are numbered from $1$ to $10$. After shuffling, two sets of $5$ cards each are formed. Determine the probability that the numbers $9$ and $10$ appear in the same set.
Determine the real values of $x$ for which $\sin(2x) - \sqrt{3}\cos(2x)$ is maximal.

Consider the square matrix $A$ whose main-diagonal entries are $1, 1 + x_1, 1 + x_2, \ldots, 1 + x_n$ and all of whose other entries equal $1$. It is known that $(x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n)$ is a geometric progression whose first term is $\dfrac{1}{2}$ and whose ratio is $4$. Determine the order of the matrix $A$ for its determinant to equal $256$.

Let $n$ be a natural number. Given that the determinant of the matrix
$$A = \begin{bmatrix} n & \log_2 2 & -\log_2\frac{1}{2} \\ n + 5 & \log_3 3^n & \log_3 243 \\ -5 & \log_5\frac{1}{125} & -\log_5 25 \end{bmatrix}$$
equals $9$, determine $n$ and also the sum of the entries of the first column of the inverse matrix $A^{-1}$.

In a plane lie a circle $\omega$ of radius $2\ \text{cm}$ and a point $P$ at distance $2\sqrt{2}\ \text{cm}$ from the centre of $\omega$. Consider the segments $\overline{PA}$ and $\overline{PB}$ tangent to $\omega$ at the points $A$ and $B$, respectively. Rotating the closed region bounded by the segments $\overline{PA}$ and $\overline{PB}$ and by the minor arc $\overset{\frown}{AB}$ about an axis through the centre of $\omega$ and perpendicular to the segment $\overline{PA}$ gives a solid of revolution. Determine:
a) The total surface area of the solid.
b) The volume of the solid.

The pairwise intersections of the lines $r : x - 3y + 3 = 0$, $s : x + 2y - 7 = 0$ and $t : x + 7y - 7 = 0$ are the vertices of a triangle that is the base of a right prism of height $2$ units of length. Determine:
a) The total surface area of the prism.
b) The volume of the prism.

Of the $n$ students of a school, each studies at least one of three subjects: Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry. It is known that $48\%$ of the students study Mathematics, $32\%$ study Chemistry and $36\%$ study Physics. It is also known that $8\%$ of the students study only Physics and Mathematics, while $4\%$ study all three subjects. The students who study only Chemistry and Physics together with those who study only Mathematics and Chemistry total $63$ students. Determine $n$.
Determine whether $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, $f(x) = \begin{cases} 3 + x^2, & x \ge 0 \\ 3 - x^2, & x < 0 \end{cases}$ is bijective and, if so, find $f^{-1} : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$.
Determine the values of $\theta \in [0, 2\pi]$ such that $\log_{\tan(\theta)} e^{\sin(\theta)} \ge 0$.

The lines $r_1$ and $r_2$ meet at the point $P$, exterior to a circle $\omega$. Determine the area of the minor sector of $\omega$ determined by the arc $\overset{\frown}{AB}$.

Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ be subsets of a universal set $U$. Of the statements:

Consider the equation in $\mathbb{C}$, $(z - 5 + 3i)^4 = 1$. If $z_0$ is the solution with the least principal argument among the four solutions, then the value of $|z_0|$ is

equals

If the real numbers $a$ and $b$ simultaneously satisfy the equations

a possible value of $\dfrac{a}{b}$ is

Consider the functions $f$ and $g$ of the real variable $x$ defined, respectively, by
$$f(x) = e^{x^2 + ax + b} \qquad \text{and} \qquad g(x) = \ln\left(\frac{ax}{3b}\right),$$
where $a$ and $b$ are real numbers. If $f(-1) = 1 = f(-2)$, then about the composite function $g \circ f$ one can state that

Consider functions $f, g, f + g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$. Of the statements:

Let $n > 6$ be a positive integer not divisible by $6$. If, in the division of $n^2$ by $6$, the quotient is an odd number, then the remainder of the division of $n$ by $6$ is

Consider the equation $\sum_{n=0}^{5} a_nx^n = 0$, in which the sum of the roots equals $-2$ and the coefficients $a_0, a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4$ and $a_5$ form, in this order, a geometric progression with $a_0 = 1$. Then $\sum_{n=0}^{5} a_n$ equals

Let $\lambda$ be a real solution of the equation $\sqrt{\lambda + 9} + \sqrt{2\lambda + 17} = 12$. Then the sum of the solutions $z$, with $\operatorname{Re} z > 0$, of the equation $z^4 = \lambda - 32$ is

Let $p$ be a probability on a finite sample space $\Omega$. If $A$ and $B$ are events of $\Omega$ such that $p(A) = \dfrac{1}{2}$, $p(B) = \dfrac{1}{3}$ and $p(A \cap B) = \dfrac{1}{4}$, the probabilities of the events $A\setminus B$, $A \cup B$ and $A^C \cup B^C$ are, respectively,

Consider the following outcomes concerning the tossing of a coin:

Consider $A \in M_{5\times 5}(\mathbb{R})$ with $\det(A) = \sqrt{6}$ and $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$. If $\det(\alpha A^tAA^t) = \sqrt{6}\,\alpha^2$, the value of $\alpha$ is

Let $a$ be a real number and $n$ the number of all distinct real solutions $x \in [0, 2\pi]$ of the equation $\cos^8 x - \sin^8 x + 4\sin^6 x = a$. Of the statements:

If $\cos 2x = \dfrac{1}{2}$, then a possible value of $\dfrac{\cot x - 1}{\csc(x - \pi) - \sec(\pi - x)}$ is

A line $r$ is tangent to a circle at a point $B$ and meets a line $s$ at a point $A$ exterior to the circle. The line $s$ passes through the centre of this circle and meets it at a point $C$ such that the angle $A\hat{B}C$ is obtuse. Then the angle $C\hat{A}B$ equals

About the parabola defined by the equation $x^2 + 2xy + y^2 - 2x + 4y + 1 = 0$ one can state that

Of the statements:
I. Two coplanar lines are concurrent;

A plane meets the edges of a trirectangular trihedral angle with vertex $V$, determining a triangle $ABC$ whose sides measure, respectively, $\sqrt{10}$, $\sqrt{17}$ and $5\ \text{cm}$. The volume, in $\text{cm}^3$, of the solid $VABC$ is

In the $xOy$ system the points $A = (2, 0)$, $B = (2, 5)$ and $C = (0, 1)$ are the vertices of a triangle inscribed in the base of a right circular cylinder of height $8$. For this cylinder, the ratio $\dfrac{\text{volume}}{\text{total surface area}}$, in units of length, equals

For $z = 1 + iy$, $y > 0$, determine all pairs $(a, y)$, $a > 1$, such that $z^{10} = a$. Write $a$ and $y$ as functions of $\operatorname{Arg} z$.

Determine the largest domain $D \subset \mathbb{R}$ of the function
$$f : D \to \mathbb{R}, \quad f(x) = \log_{x\left(\frac{\pi}{4} - x\right)}(4\sin x\cos x - 1).$$

Consider the polynomial $P(m) = am^2 - 3m - 18$, where $a \in \mathbb{R}$ is such that the sum of the roots of $P$ equals $3$. Determine the root $m$ of $P$ such that two, and only two, solutions of the equation in $x$, $x^3 + mx^2 + (m + 4)x + 5 = 0$, lie in the interval $]-2, 2[$.
How many regular tetrahedra of the same size can we distinguish using $4$ distinct colours to paint all their faces? Each face can be painted with only one colour.

Consider the system in the real variable $x$:
$$\begin{cases} x^2 - x = \alpha \\ x - x^3 = \beta. \end{cases}$$
(a) Determine the real numbers $\alpha$ and $\beta$ for which the system has only real solutions.

Consider the system in the real variables $x$ and $y$:
$$\begin{cases} x\sin\alpha + 3y\cos\alpha = a \\ x\cos\alpha + y\sin\alpha = b, \end{cases}$$
with $\alpha \in \left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right[$ and $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$. Determine for which values of $\alpha$, $a$ and $b$ the system is (i) consistent with a unique solution, (ii) consistent with infinitely many solutions, or (iii) inconsistent, respectively. Find the pairs $(\alpha, \beta) \in \left]0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right[ \times \left]0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right[$ that simultaneously satisfy the equations
$$(\tan\alpha + \cot\beta)\cos\alpha\sin\beta - 2\cos^2(\alpha - \beta) = -1 \qquad \text{and} \qquad \sqrt{3}\sin(\alpha + \beta) + \cos(\alpha + \beta) = \sqrt{3}.$$

Determine the area of the plane figure located in the first quadrant and bounded by the curves
$$(y - x - 2)\left(y + \frac{x}{2} - 2\right) = 0 \qquad \text{and} \qquad x^2 - 2x + y^2 - 8 = 0.$$

In a triangle with vertices $A$, $B$ and $C$, the altitude, the angle bisector and the median from the vertex $C$ divide the angle $B\hat{C}A$ into four equal angles. If $l$ is the length of the side opposite the vertex $C$, compute:

(b) The angles $C\hat{A}B$, $A\hat{B}C$ and $B\hat{C}A$.

The lengths of the distinct edges $AB$, $AD$ and $AE$ form an arithmetic progression whose sum is $12\ \text{cm}$. It is known that the volume of the pyramid $ABCF$ equals $10\ \text{cm}^3$. Compute:

Of the statements:
I. If $x, y \in \mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$, with $y \ne -x$, then $x + y \in \mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$;

(C) only III.
(D) only I and II.
(E) none.

If $z \in \mathbb{C}$, then $z^6 - 3|z|^4\left(z^2 - \overline{z}^2\right) - \overline{z}^6$ equals

(A) $\left(z^2 - \overline{z}^2\right)^3$.

(D) $(z - \overline{z})^6$.
(E) $(z - \overline{z})^2\left(z^4 - \overline{z}^4\right)$.

Let $z, w \in \mathbb{C}$. Of the statements:
I. $|z + w|^2 + |z - w|^2 = 2\left(|z|^2 + |w|^2\right)$;
II. $(z + \overline{w})^2 - (z - \overline{w})^2 = 4z\overline{w}$;
III. $|z + w|^2 - |z - w|^2 = 4\operatorname{Re}(z\overline{w})$,
the true one(s) is (are)

(A) only I.
(B) only I and II.
(C) only I and III.
(D) only II and III.
(E) all.

Consider the polynomials in $x \in \mathbb{R}$ of the form $p(x) = x^5 + a_3x^3 + a_2x^2 + a_1x$. The roots of $p(x) = 0$ form an arithmetic progression with common difference $\dfrac{1}{2}$ when $(a_1, a_2, a_3)$ equals

(A) $\left(\dfrac{1}{4}, 0, \dfrac{5}{4}\right)$.
(B) $\left(\dfrac{1}{4}, 1, \dfrac{5}{4}\right)$.
(C) $\left(\dfrac{1}{4}, 0, -\dfrac{5}{4}\right)$.
(D) $\left(\dfrac{5}{4}, 0, \dfrac{1}{4}\right)$.
(E) $\left(\dfrac{1}{4}, -1, -\dfrac{1}{4}\right)$.

For positive integers $k$ and $n$ with $k \le n$, it is known that $\dfrac{n+1}{k+1}\dbinom{n}{k} = \dbinom{n+1}{k+1}$. Then the value of
$$\binom{n}{0} + \frac{1}{2}\binom{n}{1} + \frac{1}{3}\binom{n}{2} + \cdots + \frac{1}{n+1}\binom{n}{n}$$
equals

(A) $2^n + 1$.
(B) $2^{n+1} + 1$.
(C) $\dfrac{2^{n+1} + 1}{n}$.
(D) $\dfrac{2^{n+1} - 1}{n+1}$.
(E) $\dfrac{2^n - 1}{n}$.

Consider the following statements about square matrices $A$ and $B$ of order $n$, with $A$ invertible and $B$ antisymmetric:
I. If the product $AB$ is invertible, then $n$ is even;
II. If the product $AB$ is not invertible, then $n$ is odd;
III. If $B$ is invertible, then $n$ is even.
Of these statements, the true one(s) is (are)

(A) only I.
(B) only I and II.
(C) only I and III.
(D) only II and III.
(E) all.

Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 & 1 \\ y & -x & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} x + 1 & x \\ y - 2 & y \\ z + 3 & z \end{bmatrix}$ be real matrices such that the product $AB$ is an antisymmetric matrix. Of the statements below:
I. $BA$ is antisymmetric;
II. $BA$ is not invertible;
III. The system $(BA)X = 0$, with $X^t = [x_1\ x_2\ x_3]$, has infinitely many solutions,
the true one(s) is (are)

(A) only I and II.
(B) only II and III.
(C) only I.
(D) only II.
(E) only III.

Let $M$ be an invertible square matrix of order $3$ satisfying the equality
$$\det(2M^2) - \det\left(\sqrt[3]{2}\,M^3\right) = \frac{2}{9}\det(3M).$$
Then a possible value for the determinant of the inverse of $M$ is

(A) $\dfrac{1}{3}$.
(B) $\dfrac{1}{2}$.
(C) $\dfrac{2}{3}$.
(D) $\dfrac{4}{5}$.
(E) $\dfrac{5}{4}$.

Consider the equation $A(t)X = B(t)$, $t \in \mathbb{R}$, where
$$A(t) = \begin{bmatrix} 2e^{-2t} & -e^{2t} & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \\ -3 & 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}, \quad X = \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} \quad \text{and} \quad B(t) = \begin{bmatrix} e^t \\ -\sqrt{2} \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}.$$
Given that $\det A(t) = 1$ and $t \ne 0$, the values of $x$, $y$ and $z$ are, respectively,

(A) $2\sqrt{2}$, $0$, $-3\sqrt{2}$.
(B) $-2\sqrt{2}$, $0$, $-3\sqrt{2}$.
(C) $0$, $3\sqrt{2}$, $2\sqrt{2}$.
(D) $0$, $2\sqrt{3}$, $\sqrt{3}$.
(E) $2\sqrt{3}$, $-\sqrt{3}$, $0$.

Consider the complex polynomial $p(z) = z^4 + az^3 + 5z^2 - iz - 6$, where $a$ is a complex constant. Given that $2i$ is one of the roots of $p(z) = 0$, the other three roots are

(A) $-3i$, $-1$, $1$.
(B) $-i$, $i$, $1$.
(C) $-i$, $i$, $-1$.
(D) $-2i$, $-1$, $1$.
(E) $-2i$, $-i$, $i$.

Given that $\sin x = \dfrac{2ab}{a^2 + b^2}$, $a \ne 0$ and $b \ne 0$, a possible value for $\csc 2x - \dfrac{1}{2}\tan x$ is

(A) $\dfrac{a - b}{ab}$.
(B) $\dfrac{a + b}{2ab}$.
(C) $\dfrac{a^2 - b^2}{ab}$.
(D) $\dfrac{a^2 + b^2}{4ab}$.
(E) $\dfrac{a^2 - b^2}{4ab}$.

Consider the triangle $ABC$ right-angled at $A$. Let $\overline{AE}$ and $\overline{AD}$ be the altitude and the median to the hypotenuse $\overline{BC}$, respectively. If the length of $\overline{BE}$ is $(\sqrt{2} - 1)\ \text{cm}$ and the length of $\overline{AD}$ is $1\ \text{cm}$, then $\overline{AC}$ measures, in cm,

(A) $4\sqrt{2} - 5$.
(B) $3 - \sqrt{2}$.
(C) $\sqrt{6 - 2\sqrt{2}}$.
(D) $3(\sqrt{2} - 1)$.
(E) $3\sqrt{4\sqrt{2} - 5}$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with vertices $A = (1, 4)$, $B = (5, 1)$ and $C = (5, 5)$. The radius of the circumcircle of the triangle measures, in units of length,

(A) $\dfrac{15}{8}$.
(B) $\dfrac{5\sqrt{17}}{4}$.
(C) $\dfrac{3\sqrt{17}}{5}$.
(D) $\dfrac{5\sqrt{17}}{8}$.
(E) $\dfrac{17\sqrt{5}}{8}$.

In an isosceles triangle $ABC$ whose area measures $48\ \text{cm}^2$, the ratio between the lengths of the altitude $\overline{AP}$ and the base $\overline{BC}$ equals $\dfrac{2}{3}$. Of the statements below:
I. The medians to the sides $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{AC}$ measure $\sqrt{97}\ \text{cm}$;
II. The centroid is at distance $4\ \text{cm}$ from the vertex $A$;
III. If $\alpha$ is the angle formed by the base $\overline{BC}$ with the median $\overline{BM}$ to the side $\overline{AC}$, then $\cos\alpha = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{97}}$,
the true one(s) is (are)

(A) only I.
(B) only II.
(C) only III.
(D) only I and III.
(E) only II and III.

Consider the trapezium $ABCD$ with bases $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{CD}$. Let $M$ and $N$ be the midpoints of the diagonals $\overline{AC}$ and $\overline{BD}$, respectively. Then, if $\overline{AB}$ has length $x$ and $\overline{CD}$ has length $y < x$, the length of $\overline{MN}$ equals

(A) $x - y$.
(B) $\dfrac{1}{2}(x - y)$.
(C) $\dfrac{1}{3}(x - y)$.
(D) $\dfrac{1}{3}(x + y)$.
(E) $\dfrac{1}{4}(x + y)$.

A pyramid of height $h = 1\ \text{cm}$ and volume $V = 50\ \text{cm}^3$ has as its base a convex polygon with $n$ sides. From one of the vertices of the polygon, $n - 3$ diagonals are drawn that decompose it into $n - 2$ triangles whose areas $S_i$, $i = 1, 2, \ldots, n - 2$, form an arithmetic progression in which $S_3 = \dfrac{3}{2}\ \text{cm}^2$ and $S_6 = 3\ \text{cm}^2$. Then $n$ equals

(A) $22$.
(B) $24$.
(C) $26$.
(D) $28$.
(E) $32$.

The equation of the circle located in the first quadrant that has area equal to $4\pi$ (units of area) and is tangent simultaneously to the lines $r : 2x - 2y + 5 = 0$ and $s : x + y - 4 = 0$ is

(A) $\left(x - \frac{3}{4}\right)^2 + \left(y - \frac{10}{4}\right)^2 = 4$.
(B) $\left(x - \frac{3}{4}\right)^2 + \left(y - \left(2\sqrt{2} + \frac{3}{4}\right)\right)^2 = 4$.
(C) $\left(x - \left(2\sqrt{2} + \frac{3}{4}\right)\right)^2 + \left(y - \frac{10}{4}\right)^2 = 4$.
(D) $\left(x - \left(2\sqrt{2} + \frac{3}{4}\right)\right)^2 + \left(y - \frac{13}{4}\right)^2 = 4$.
(E) $\left(x - \left(2\sqrt{2} + \frac{3}{4}\right)\right)^2 + \left(y - \frac{11}{4}\right)^2 = 4$.

Consider the solid of revolution obtained by rotating an isosceles triangle $ABC$ about a line parallel to the base $\overline{BC}$ that is at distance $0.25\ \text{cm}$ from the vertex $A$ and $0.75\ \text{cm}$ from the base $\overline{BC}$. If the side $\overline{AB}$ measures $\dfrac{\sqrt{\pi^2 + 1}}{2\pi}\ \text{cm}$, the volume of this solid, in $\text{cm}^3$, equals

(A) $\dfrac{9}{16}$.
(B) $\dfrac{13}{96}$.
(C) $\dfrac{7}{24}$.
(D) $\dfrac{9}{24}$.
(E) $\dfrac{11}{96}$.

Consider the functions $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, $f(x) = e^{\alpha x}$, where $\alpha$ is a positive real constant, and $g : [0, \infty[ \to \mathbb{R}$, $g(x) = \sqrt{x}$. Determine the solution set of the inequality
$$(g \circ f)(x) > (f \circ g)(x).$$

Determine the real solutions of the equation in $x$
$$\left(\log_4 x\right)^3 - \log_4\left(x^4\right) - 3\,\frac{\log_{10} 16x}{\log_{100} 16} = 0.$$

a) Determine the maximum value of $|z + i|$, given that $|z - 2| = 1$, $z \in \mathbb{C}$.
b) If $z_0 \in \mathbb{C}$ satisfies (a), determine $z_0$.
Determine how many different rectangular parallelepipeds can be built such that the length of each of their edges is a positive integer not exceeding $10$.

Consider the linear system in the unknowns $x$, $y$ and $z$
$$\begin{cases} x + y + 2z = 0 \\ -x + (\sin\theta)\,y + 4z = 0 \\ 2x + (1 - \cos 2\theta)\,y + 16z = 0 \end{cases}, \qquad \theta \in [0, 2\pi].$$
a) Determine $\theta$ such that the system has infinitely many solutions.
b) For $\theta$ found in (a), determine the solution set of the system.

Determine the set of all values of $x \in [0, 2\pi]$ that satisfy simultaneously
$$\frac{2\sin^2 x + \sin x - 1}{\cos x - 1} < 0 \qquad \text{and} \qquad \tan x + \sqrt{3} < \left(1 + \sqrt{3}\cot x\right)\cot x.$$

Six spheres of the same radius $R$ are placed on a horizontal surface in such a way that their centres are the vertices of a regular hexagon with edge $2R$. On top of these spheres a seventh sphere of radius $2R$ is placed, tangent to all the others. Determine the distance from the centre of the seventh sphere to the horizontal surface.

A right cylinder of height $h = 1\ \text{cm}$ has its base in the $xy$-plane given by
$$x^2 + y^2 - 2x - 4y + 4 \le 0.$$
A plane containing the line $y - x = 0$ and parallel to the axis of the cylinder cuts it into two solids. Compute the total surface area of the smaller solid.

Consider the following statements about real numbers:
I. If the decimal expansion of $x$ is infinite and periodic, then $x$ is a rational number.
II. $\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(\sqrt{2} - 1)\sqrt{2^n}} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{1 - 2\sqrt{2}}$.
III. $\ln\sqrt[3]{e^2} + (\log_3 2)(\log_4 9)$ is a rational number.
The true one(s) is (are):

(A) none.
(B) only II.
(C) only I and II.
(D) only I and III.
(E) I, II and III.

Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ be the subsets of $\mathbb{C}$ defined by $A = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z + 2 - 3i| < \sqrt{19}\}$, $B = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z + i| < 7/2\}$ and $C = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : z^2 + 6z + 10 = 0\}$. Then $(A\setminus B) \cap C$ is the set

(A) $\{-1 - 3i, -1 + 3i\}$.
(B) $\{-3 - i, -3 + i\}$.
(C) $\{-3 + i\}$.
(D) $\{-3 - i\}$.
(E) $\{-1 + 3i\}$.

If $z = \left(\dfrac{1 + \sqrt{3}i}{1 - \sqrt{3}i}\right)^{10}$, then the value of $2\arcsin(\operatorname{Re}(z)) + 5\arctan(2\operatorname{Im}(z))$ equals

(A) $-\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$.
(B) $-\dfrac{\pi}{3}$.
(C) $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$.
(D) $\dfrac{4\pi}{3}$.
(E) $\dfrac{5\pi}{3}$.

Let $C$ be a circle tangent simultaneously to the lines $r : 3x + 4y - 4 = 0$ and $s : 3x + 4y - 19 = 0$. The area of the disc bounded by $C$ equals

(A) $\dfrac{5\pi}{7}$.
(B) $\dfrac{4\pi}{5}$.
(C) $\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$.
(D) $\dfrac{8\pi}{3}$.
(E) $\dfrac{9\pi}{4}$.

Let $(a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots)$ be the sequence defined as follows: $a_1 = 1$, $a_2 = 1$ and $a_n = a_{n-1} + a_{n-2}$ for $n \ge 3$. Consider the following statements:
I. There are three consecutive terms $a_p, a_{p+1}, a_{p+2}$ that, in this order, form a geometric progression.
II. $a_7$ is a prime number.
III. If $n$ is a multiple of $3$, then $a_n$ is even.
The true one(s) is (are)

(A) only II.
(B) only I and II.
(C) only I and III.
(D) only II and III.
(E) I, II and III.

Consider the equation $\dfrac{a}{1 - x^2} - \dfrac{b}{x - 1/2} = 5$, with $a$ and $b$ positive integers. Of the statements:
I. If $a = 1$ and $b = 2$, then $x = 0$ is a solution of the equation.
II. If $x$ is a solution of the equation, then $x \ne \dfrac{1}{2}$, $x \ne -1$ and $x \ne 1$.
III. $x = \dfrac{2}{3}$ cannot be a solution of the equation.
The true one(s) is (are)

(A) only II.
(B) only I and II.
(C) only I and III.
(D) only II and III.
(E) I, II and III.

Consider the polynomial $p$ given by $p(x) = 2x^3 + ax^2 + bx - 16$, with $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$. Given that $p$ has a double root and that $2$ is a root of $p$, the value of $b - a$ equals

(A) $-36$.
(B) $-12$.
(C) $6$.
(D) $12$.
(E) $24$.

Let $p$ be the polynomial given by $p(x) = \sum_{j=0}^{15} a_jx^j$, with $a_j \in \mathbb{R}$, $j = 0, 1, \ldots, 15$, and $a_{15} \ne 0$. Given that $i$ is a root of $p$ and that $p(2) = 1$, the remainder of the division of $p$ by the polynomial $q$ given by $q(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - 2$ equals

(A) $\dfrac{1}{5}x^2 - \dfrac{1}{5}$.
(B) $\dfrac{1}{5}x^2 + \dfrac{1}{5}$.
(C) $\dfrac{2}{5}x^2 + \dfrac{2}{5}$.
(D) $\dfrac{3}{5}x^2 - \dfrac{3}{5}$.
(E) $\dfrac{3}{5}x^2 + \dfrac{1}{5}$.

Consider all right triangles with sides measuring $\sqrt{a}$, $2\sqrt{a}$ and $a$. Among these triangles, the one with the largest hypotenuse has its smallest angle, in radians, equal to

(A) $\arctan\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}$.
(B) $\arctan\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$.
(C) $\arctan\dfrac{1}{2}$.
(D) $\arctan\dfrac{3}{5}$.
(E) $\arctan\dfrac{4}{5}$.

The values of $x \in [0, 2\pi]$ that satisfy the equation $2\sin x - \cos x = 1$ are

(A) $\arccos\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)$ and $\pi$.
(B) $\arcsin\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)$ and $\pi$.
(C) $\arcsin\left(-\dfrac{4}{5}\right)$ and $\pi$.
(D) $\arccos\left(-\dfrac{4}{5}\right)$ and $\pi$.
(E) $\arccos\left(\dfrac{4}{5}\right)$ and $\pi$.

Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be real numbers such that $\alpha, \beta, \alpha + \beta \in\ ]0, 2\pi[$ and that satisfy the equations
$$\cos^2\frac{\alpha}{2} = \frac{4}{5}\cos^4\frac{\alpha}{2} + \frac{1}{5} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \cos^2\frac{\beta}{3} = \frac{4}{7}\cos^4\frac{\beta}{3} + \frac{3}{7}.$$
Then the least value of $\cos(\alpha + \beta)$ equals

(A) $-1$.
(B) $-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.
(C) $-\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$.
(D) $-\dfrac{1}{2}$.
(E) $0$.

Let $A = (a_{ij})_{5\times 5}$ be the matrix such that $a_{ij} = 2^{i-1}(2j - 1)$, $1 \le i, j \le 5$. Consider the following statements:
I. The entries of each row $i$ form an arithmetic progression with common difference $2^i$.
II. The entries of each column $j$ form a geometric progression with ratio $2$.
III. $\operatorname{tr} A$ is a prime number.
The true one(s) is (are)

(A) only I.
(B) only I and II.
(C) only II and III.
(D) only I and III.
(E) I, II and III.

Consider the matrix $M = (m_{ij})_{2\times 2}$ such that $m_{ij} = j - i + 1$, $i, j = 1, 2$. Given that
$$\det\left(\sum_{k=1}^{n}M^k - n\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\right) = 252,$$
the value of $n$ equals

(A) $4$.
(B) $5$.
(C) $6$.
(D) $7$.
(E) $8$.

Consider the points $A = (0, -1)$, $B = (0, 5)$ and the line $r : 2x - 3y + 6 = 0$. Of the following statements:
I. $d(A, r) = d(B, r)$.
II. $B$ is the reflection of $A$ in the line $r$.
III. $\overline{AB}$ is the base of an equilateral triangle $ABC$ with vertex $C = (-3\sqrt{3}, 2)$ or $C = (3\sqrt{3}, 2)$.
the true one(s) is (are) only

(A) I.
(B) II.
(C) I and II.
(D) I and III.
(E) II and III.

Given the point $A = \left(4, \dfrac{25}{6}\right)$ and the line $r : 3x + 4y - 12 = 0$, consider the triangle with vertices $ABC$ whose base $\overline{BC}$ lies on $r$ and whose sides $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{AC}$ both measure $\dfrac{25}{6}$. Then the area and the perimeter of this triangle are, respectively,

(A) $\dfrac{22}{3}$ and $\dfrac{40}{3}$.
(B) $\dfrac{23}{3}$ and $\dfrac{40}{3}$.
(C) $\dfrac{25}{3}$ and $\dfrac{31}{3}$.
(D) $\dfrac{25}{3}$ and $\dfrac{35}{3}$.
(E) $\dfrac{25}{3}$ and $\dfrac{40}{3}$.

Consider the following statements:
I. The locus of the midpoint of a segment $\overline{AB}$ of fixed length $l$ whose endpoints move freely on the coordinate axes is a circle.
II. The locus of the points $(x, y)$ such that $6x^3 + x^2y - xy^2 - 4x^2 - 2xy = 0$ is a finite set in the Cartesian plane $\mathbb{R}^2$.
III. The points $(2, 3)$, $(4, -1)$ and $(3, 1)$ lie on a circle.
Of these, the true one(s) is (are)

(A) only I.
(B) only II.
(C) only III.
(D) I and II.
(E) I and III.

Let $ABCD$ be an isosceles trapezium with longer base $\overline{AB}$ measuring $15$, side $\overline{AD}$ measuring $9$ and right angle $A\hat{D}B$. The distance between the side $\overline{AB}$ and the point $E$ where the diagonals meet is

(A) $\dfrac{21}{8}$.
(B) $\dfrac{27}{8}$.
(C) $\dfrac{35}{8}$.
(D) $\dfrac{37}{8}$.
(E) $\dfrac{45}{8}$.

In a triangle $PQR$, consider the points $M$ and $N$ on the sides $\overline{PQ}$ and $\overline{PR}$, respectively, such that the segment $\overline{MN}$ is tangent to the incircle of the triangle $PQR$. Given that the perimeter of the triangle $PQR$ is $25$ and that the length of $\overline{QR}$ is $10$, the perimeter of the triangle $PMN$ equals

(A) $5$.
(B) $6$.
(C) $8$.
(D) $10$.
(E) $15$.

Consider a circle $C$, in the first quadrant, tangent to the axis $Ox$ and to the line $r : x - y = 0$. Given that the power of the point $O = (0, 0)$ with respect to this circle equals $4$, the centre and the radius of $C$ are, respectively,

(A) $(2, 2\sqrt{2} - 2)$ and $2\sqrt{2} - 2$.
(B) $\left(2, \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$ and $\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}$.
(C) $(2, \sqrt{2} - 1)$ and $\sqrt{2} - 1$.
(D) $(2, 2 - \sqrt{2})$ and $2 - \sqrt{2}$.
(E) $(2, 4\sqrt{2} - 4)$ and $4\sqrt{2} - 4$.

A cup in the shape of a right circular cone contains a certain volume of liquid whose surface is at distance $h$ from the vertex of the cone. If an identical volume of liquid is added to the cup, the surface of the liquid will rise, relative to the original one, by

(A) $\sqrt[3]{2} - h$.
(B) $\sqrt[3]{2} - 1$.
(C) $(\sqrt[3]{2} - 1)h$.
(D) $h$.
(E) $\dfrac{h}{2}$.

Consider the functions $f_1, f_2, f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, where $f_1(x) = \frac{1}{2}|x| + 3$, $f_2(x) = \frac{3}{2}|x + 1|$ and $f(x)$ is the larger of $f_1(x)$ and $f_2(x)$, for each $x \in \mathbb{R}$. Determine:
a) All $x \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $f_1(x) = f_2(x)$.
b) The least value taken by the function $f$.
c) All solutions of the equation $f(x) = 5$.

Consider the polynomial $p$ given by $p(z) = 18z^3 + \beta z^2 - 7z - \beta$, where $\beta$ is a real number.
a) Determine all values of $\beta$ given that $p$ has a root of modulus $1$ with nonzero imaginary part.
b) For each value of $\beta$ obtained in a), determine all the roots of the polynomial $p$.
Let $M \subset \mathbb{R}$ be given by $M = \{|z^2 + az - 1| : z \in \mathbb{C} \text{ and } |z| = 1\}$, with $a \in \mathbb{R}$. Determine the largest element of $M$ as a function of $a$.

Let $S$ be the set of all polynomials of degree $4$ that have three of their coefficients equal to $2$ and the other two equal to $1$.
a) Determine the number of elements of $S$.
b) Determine the subset of $S$ consisting of the polynomials that have $-1$ as one of their roots.

Three people, here called $A$, $B$ and $C$, carry out the following experiment: $A$ receives a blank card and marks on it the sign $+$ or the sign $-$, then passes it to $B$, who keeps or changes the sign marked by $A$ and passes the card on to $C$. $C$, in turn, also chooses to keep or change the sign on the card. Given that the probability that $A$ writes the sign $+$ is $1/3$ and that the respective probabilities that $B$ and $C$ change the sign received are $2/3$, determine the probability that $A$ wrote the sign $+$, given that this was the sign at the end of the experiment.

Let $n$ be a positive integer such that $\sin\dfrac{\pi}{2n} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 - \sqrt{3}}{4}}$.
a) Determine $n$.
b) Determine $\sin\dfrac{\pi}{24}$.

Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be nonzero real numbers. Determine the values of $b, c, d$, as well as the relation between $\alpha$ and $\beta$, for which both linear systems $S$ and $T$ below are consistent with infinitely many solutions.
$$S \begin{cases} 2x + by = \alpha \\ cx + y = \beta \end{cases} \qquad\qquad T \begin{cases} cx + 3y = \alpha \\ 4x + dy = \beta \end{cases}$$
It is known that the equation $3x^2 + 5xy - 2y^2 - 3x + 8y - 6 = 0$ represents the union of two intersecting lines $r$ and $s$ forming an acute angle $\theta$. Determine the tangent of $\theta$.

To build a tetrahedron, a rectangular sheet of paper with sides $3\ \text{cm}$ and $4\ \text{cm}$ is folded along one of its diagonals so that the two parts of the sheet form a right angle and constitute two faces of the tetrahedron. In a second step, the remaining faces are suitably completed with other paper to form the tetrahedron. Obtain the lengths of the edges of the tetrahedron.

Consider the following statements:
I. The function $f(x) = \log_{10}\left(\frac{x-1}{x}\right)$ is strictly increasing on the interval $]1, +\infty[$.
II. The equation $2^{x+2} = 3^{x-1}$ has a unique real solution.
III. The equation $(x + 1)^x = x$ has at least one positive real solution.
The true one(s) is (are)

(A) only I.
(B) only I and II.
(C) only II and III.
(D) I, II and III.
(E) only III.

If $x$ is a natural number with $2015$ digits, then the number of digits of the integer part of $\sqrt[7]{x}$ equals

(A) $285$.
(B) $286$.
(C) $287$.
(D) $288$.
(E) $289$.

Choosing at random three distinct integers in the interval $[1, 20]$, the probability that they are, in some order, in geometric progression equals

(A) $\dfrac{2}{285}$.
(B) $\dfrac{2}{217}$.
(C) $\dfrac{1}{190}$.
(D) $\dfrac{4}{225}$.
(E) $\dfrac{1}{380}$.

The central circle, painted red, has radius $\alpha$ units. Each subsequent circle has radius one unit greater than the previous one: $\alpha+1$, then $\alpha+2$ and so on. Determine the total red area in terms of $\alpha$, given that the target has $33$ circles.

Four identical spheres, pairwise tangent, are simultaneously inscribed in a single larger sphere, in such a way that the centres of the smaller spheres form a regular tetrahedron. Compute the ratio between the volume of the larger sphere and the sum of the volumes of the four smaller spheres.

Given the real numbers $\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\ldots,\alpha_{n-1}$, define the matrices $A=(a_{ij})$ and $B=(b_{ij})$, both of order $n\times n$, by
$$a_{ij}=\begin{cases}0, & \text{if } j\ge i,\\ \alpha_j^{\,i-j-1}, & \text{if } j<i\end{cases}\qquad b_{ij}=\begin{cases}1, & \text{if } j\ge i,\\ 0, & \text{if } j<i\end{cases}$$
Suppose that the sum of the entries of column $j$ of the matrix $AB$ equals $n-j$.
a) Determine the determinant of $AB$.
b) Determine the trace of $AB$ in terms of $n$.
c) Assuming that $n=5$, determine all possible values of $\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3,\alpha_4\in\mathbb{R}$.

Let $p(x)$ be a polynomial of degree four with real coefficients. The sum of the roots of $p(x)$ is $\dfrac{3}{2}$, and their product is $-\dfrac{5}{2}$. Determine all the roots of $p(x)$ in $\mathbb{C}$, given that the remainder of the division of $p(x)$ by $x^3-x+4$ equals $9x^2-4x+7$.
